effect: A dual word-form ending in ī, ū or e is named pragṛhya, so that 6.1.125 keeps it unchanged before a vowel.
sthanin: no sound is replaced; a samjna is given to a dual (dvivacana) word-form whose last sound is ī, ū or e (harī, viṣṇū, gaṅge, pacete, pacethe)
nimitta: the word is a dual (case dual of an i/u/ā-stem, or a verbal dual ending in e) and ends in a LONG ī, ū or e
conditions: Sutra text 'īdūdeddvivacanaṃ pragṛhyam' with tadantavidhi: Kasika 'ईत् ऊत् एत् इत्येवमन्तं द्विवचनं शब्दरूपं प्रगृह्यसंज्ञं भवति'; Balamanorama: 'ईदूदेदिति द्विवचनविशेषणत्वात्तदन्तविधिः' (needed so that pacete counts: 'तदन्तविध्यभावे ... पचेते इत्यत्र ... एद्रूपत्वाभावात्प्रगृह्यत्वं न स्यात्').

'dvivacanam' is the word-form's number, and is NOT extended to endings that were elided (pratyayalakṣaṇa, 1.1.62): Tattvabodhini 'संज्ञाविधौ प्रत्ययग्रहणे तदन्तग्रहणं नास्ति' (inferred from 'सुप्तिङन्तम्' 1.4.14); Mahabhasya on 1.1.19 'न प्रगृह्यसञ्ज्ञायां प्रत्ययलक्षणं भवति'. Hence kumāryoḥ agāram -> kumāryagāram, vadhvagāram (yaṇ).
Kasika 'ईदूदेदिति किम्? वृक्षावत्र। प्लक्षावत्र' - a dual in au/other endings is not pragṛhya. 'द्विवचनमिति किम्? कुमार्यत्र। किशोर्यत्र' - a singular in ī is not pragṛhya.

The vowels are given with the tapara marker ('तपरकरणमसंदेहार्थम्', Kasika; Mahabhasya: 'तपरस्तत्कालस्येति तत्कालानां सवर्णानां ग्रहणं यथा स्यात्' - so udātta/anudātta/svarita long vowels are all included) and are LONG: Mahabhasya shows short i is excluded ('अकुर्वहि अत्र, अकुर्वह्यत्रेति').

Pluta ī/ū/e are included by a jñāpaka in 6.1.125 (Mahabhasya on 1.1.11: 'सिद्धः प्लुतः स्वरसन्धिषु' because 6.1.125 says 'प्लुतः प्रकृत्या'), and by the samjna being 'kāryakāla' (Mahabhasya: 'कार्यकालं सञ्ज्ञापरिभाषम्। यत्र कार्यं तत्रोपस्थितं द्रष्टव्यम्').
The ī/ū of a dual counts as a dual even when it is the ekādeśa of i/u + au (harī = hari + au): Balamanorama on 1.1.12 'ईकारस्य परादिवत्त्वाश्रयणाद्द्विवचनत्वम्' (para-ādivat, 6.1.85).

exceptions_and_blockers.note: pratyayalakṣaṇa does not operate for pragṛhya-samjna: Mahabhasya on 1.1.19 'न प्रगृह्यसञ्ज्ञायां प्रत्ययलक्षणं भवति' (jñāpaka from 1.4.14 sup-tiṅ-antam).
tapara: long vowels of the same duration only (Mahabhasya on this sutra: taparas tatkālasya gives savarṇa of the same length; short ī/ū are not pragṛhya).
the ī/ū after m of adas is covered separately, because masculine amū and plural amī are not duals of the kind this sutra sees (Balamanorama on 1.1.12).

ordering_notes: Mahabhasya: the samjna is 'kāryakāla' - it is looked up at the moment the pragṛhya-dependent rule (6.1.125, 8.4.57 ...) operates ('यत्र कार्यं तत्रोपस्थितं द्रष्टव्यम्'), not at the moment the word is formed. The ī/ū/e must be present in the word AS IT STANDS at that moment; 8.2.1 makes tripādī products invisible, which is why 1.1.12 exists for amī/amū (see there).

effect: The ī and ū that stand after the m of adas (amī, amū) are named pragṛhya, although amī is a plural and masculine amū owes its ū to an asiddha rule.
sthanin: no sound is replaced; samjna for ī/ū following the m (substitute of d, 8.2.80) of adas
nimitta: the sound is ī or ū and immediately follows the m that is part of the word adas: amī (nom. pl. masc.), amū (nom. dual masc.)
conditions: Kasika 'अदसः सम्बन्धी यो मकारस्तस्मात् पर ईदूदेतः प्रगृह्यसंज्ञा भवन्ति ... एकारस्य नास्त्युदाहरणम्'. Balamanorama: 'अदस' is an avayava-ṣaṣṭhī ('अदश्शब्दावयवान्मकारात्'), 'māt' is a pañcamī of direction (so 'after m'); 'ईदूत्' continue but 'eṭ' and 'dvivacanam' do NOT ('एदिति नानुवर्तते, अदश्शब्दे मकारात्परस्यैकारस्याऽसंभवात्'; 'द्विवचनमित्यपि नानुवर्तते ... अमी इति बहुवचनत्वात्').

'adaso iti kim? śamyatra, dāḍimyatra' (Kasika): only the ī/ū of adas. 'mād iti kim? amuke \'tra' (Kasika/Laghu): the e of amuke (adas + akac) is not right after the m, and without the word 'māt' the anuvṛtti of 'eṭ' would make it pragṛhya (Kaumudi 'असति माद्ग्रहणे एकारोऽप्यनुवर्तेत'; Balamanorama gives the mechanism of the anuvṛtti).

For feminine/neuter amū the earlier sutra 1.1.11 already works (their ū is the e-substitute of a real dual); masculine amū (adau -> amū) needs this sutra: Balamanorama 'रामकृष्णावमू' chosen because 'पुंसि पूर्वेण न सिध्यति, औकारान्तत्वात्' (Tattvabodhini).

exceptions_and_blockers.note: 8.2.80 (adaso 'ser dād u do maḥ) and 8.2.81 (eta īd bahuvacane) are tripādī rules and produce the m, ī, ū; they are asiddha for sapādasaptādhyāyī rules, but not for this samjna: Balamanorama 'अदसो मादिति सूत्रं प्रति तु उत्वमत्वे नासिद्धे, आरम्भसामर्थ्यात्'.

ordering_notes: Mahabhasya on this sutra: 'मात्प्रगृह्यसञ्ज्ञायां तस्यासिद्धत्वादयावेकादेशप्रतिषेधः' (the objection that the ayādi/ekādeśa might apply first because ī/ū/m are asiddha), answered by 'आश्रयात् सिद्धत्वं च यथा रोरुत्वे' and by the later yoga-vibhāga ('अदसः / मात्') so that the samjna is looked up after the tripādī substitutions have been made ('न चात्रेत्वोत्वे स्तः। नापि मकारः। उभयमप्यसिद्धम्' is the problem, and the solution is that these rules are siddha by āśraya for this purpose). Tattvabodhini: 'अदसो मादिति सूत्रं प्रति मूत्वमीत्वं च नाऽसिद्धम्, आरम्भसामर्थ्यात्'. Result: the engine must feed the tripādī output (amī, amū) into 1.1.12.

effect: The Vedic substitute śe (the e that replaces a case ending, as in asme, yuṣme, tve, me) is pragṛhya.
sthanin: no sound is replaced; samjna for the e-substitute (śe) of a sup ending
nimitta: the word-final e is the śe-ādeśa of the case ending (7.1.39 supāṃ sulukpūrvasavarṇā''ccheyāḍāḍyāyājālaḥ) - asme (= asmabhyam), yuṣme, tve, me
conditions: Kasika: 'शे इत्येतत् प्रगृह्यसंज्ञं भवति। किमिदं शे इति? सुपामादेशश्छन्दसि [७.१.३९]'. Tattvabodhini: 'सुपां सुलुगिति भ्यसः शेआदेशः। शेषे लोपः'.

Kasika: 'छान्दसमेतदेवैकमुदाहरणम् अस्मे इन्द्राबृहस्पती (ऋ० ४.४९.४) इति ... इतरत्तु लौकिकमनुकरणम्' (yuṣme iti, asme iti, tve iti, me iti are lauka quotations of pada-forms). Tattvabodhini: 'छान्दसमपीदं सन्दर्भशुद्ध्यर्थमुक्तम्'.
Only the e that IS the śe-ādeśa: an ordinary e is unaffected.

overrides.note: as a pragṛhya (through 6.1.125) the e is not turned into ay before a vowel (asme indrābṛhaspatī, not *asmay indrābṛhaspatī).

ordering_notes: Applies on the finished word; the śe-substitution (7.1.39) is sapādasaptādhyāyī, so it is siddha for 6.1.125.
notes: ENGINE: the flag vocabulary has no marker for 'e that is the śe-ādeśa'; gold cases use stem:asmad / stem:yuṣmad / stem:tvad plus 'arsa' as the nearest indicators. Only the derivation of the word (7.1.39) can tell the engine that the e is śe. The sutra is not in Laghu.

effect: A nipāta that is a single vowel (a, i, u, ṛ, ḷ, e, ai, o, au) is pragṛhya, except the ṅit particle ā (āṅ).
sthanin: no sound is replaced; samjna for a nipāta consisting of exactly one vowel-letter
nimitta: the word is a nipāta (1.4.56-58 cādi/prādi lists) that consists of ONE vowel and nothing else, and is not the ṅit ā
conditions: Kasika: 'निपातो य एकाच् आङ्वर्जितः स प्रगृह्यसंज्ञो भवति'. 'ekāc' is a karmadhāraya (eka + ac, 'the one vowel itself'), not a bahuvrīhi: Balamanorama 'एकोऽच् यस्येति बहुव्रीहिस्तु नाश्रितः, तथा सति प्रेदमित्यादावतिप्रसङ्गात्'; Mahabhasya on this sutra 'एकाजिति नायं बहुव्रीहिः'.
'nipāta iti kim? cakārātra, jahārātra'; 'ekāj iti kim? prāgnaye vācamīraya'; 'anāṅ iti kim? ā udakāntāt odakāntāt' (Kasika).

The particle ā is pragṛhya when it is aṅit (ṅ-less): 'वाक्यस्मरणयोरङित्' - ā evaṃ nu manyase, ā evaṃ kila tat. It is NOT when it is ṅit (īṣadarthe, maryādā, abhividhi): Kasika/Kaumudi/Laghu quoting the Mahabhasya kārikā 'ईषदर्थे क्रियायोगे मर्यादाभिविधौ च यः। एतमातं ङितं विद्याद्वाक्यस्मरणयोरङित्'.
Balamanorama on the meaning of the examples: 'इ विस्मये' (i = surprise), 'उ वितर्के' (u = doubt); ā in 'ā evaṃ nu manyase' signals a change of mind, in 'ā evaṃ kila tat' a recollection.

Members of the cādi list (Vidyut ganapatha, corpus.ganas_for('1.4.57'), 155 items, open_ended) that are a single vowel: a, i, u, ṛ, ḷ, u, e, ai, o, au (u occurs twice). The prādi list (1.4.58) contains 'āṅ', the one prādi that would be ekāc; it is excluded by 'anāṅ' when it is the ṅit ā.

exceptions_and_blockers.note: āṅ (the ṅit ā of the prādi list) is excluded by 'anāṅ'; Kasika/Laghu: ā īṣaduṣṇam -> oṣṇam (guṇa) because ṅit ā is not pragṛhya.

the particle uñ (u with the marker ñ) is a separate item with an OPTIONAL pragṛhya status (Śākalya) before iti (Mahabhasya on 1.1.17 'द्वावुकाराविमौ। एकोऽननुबन्धकः। अपरः सानुबन्धकः'); the plain nipāta u is nitya pragṛhya by this sutra.
the pragṛhya uñ after a may-letter can be replaced by v (a tripādī rule): Balamanorama 'प्रकृतिभावे प्राप्ते वत्ववचनम्'.

ordering_notes: Requires the nipāta samjna (1.4.57/1.4.58) to have been given first; the pragṛhya status is then used by 6.1.125.

effect: A nipāta ending in o is pragṛhya.
sthanin: no sound is replaced; samjna for a nipāta whose last sound is o
nimitta: the word is a nipāta (cādi/prādi) and ends in o: aho, āho, utāho, ho, atho, no, and the lone o
conditions: Kasika: 'निपात इति वर्तते। तस्यौकारेण तदन्तविधिः। ओदन्तो यो निपातः स प्रगृह्यसंज्ञो भवति। आहो इति। उताहो इति'.
o-ending members of the cādi list (computed from the Vidyut gana): o, āho, utāho, ho, aho, no, atho.

Mahabhasya: the examples āho, utāho are unnecessary (āha u = āho are already covered as a 'nipātasamāhāra' by 1.1.14); the sutra is justified as a prohibition-type rule; it proposes 'ओ षु यातं मरुतः' (o ṣu yātaṃ marutaḥ) as Vedic instances.

Vartika (Mahabhasya) 'ओतश्च्वि प्रतिषेधः': the o-final form made by the cvi affix (adaḥ abhavat -> ado 'bhavat) is excluded; the Mahabhasya then argues this is unnecessary because 'लक्षणप्रतिपदोक्तयोः प्रतिपदोक्तस्य' and 'गौणमुख्ययोर्मुख्ये कार्यसम्प्रत्ययः' (the o must be a real nipāta).

exceptions_and_blockers.note: the item must first be a nipāta; cvi-formed o-forms and case forms like 'go' are not (Mahabhasya 'अनदः अदः अभवत् अदोऽभवत्').

notes: Asymmetry to remember: o-ending nipātas are pragṛhya (this sutra) but the e-ending ones (he, are, aye, manye ...) are not (see 1.1.14 notes); aho/aha etc. before a vowel: pragṛhya blocks 6.1.78 (aho īśāḥ).

effect: According to Śākalya, the o that comes from the vocative (viṣṇo, vāyo, bhāno) is optionally pragṛhya before the non-Vedic quotation particle iti.
sthanin: no sound is replaced; optional samjna for the vocative o
nimitta: the o arises from the vocative singular (sambuddhi: guṇa of the stem-final u) and the next word is the non-Vedic (anārṣa) iti
conditions: Kasika: 'संबुद्धिनिमित्तो य ओकारः स शाकल्यस्याचार्यस्य मतेन प्रगृह्यसंज्ञो भवति, इति शब्देऽनार्षेऽवैदिके परतः'; 'शाकल्यग्रहणं विभाषार्थम्'.
Counter-examples: 'सम्बुद्धाविति किम्? गवित्ययमाह' (go quoted, not a vocative); 'इताविति किम्? वायोऽत्र'; 'अनार्ष इति किम्? एता गा ब्रह्मबन्ध इत्यब्रवीत्' (the iti of the Vedic text itself).
Balamanorama: 'अत्र ओदन्तत्वेऽपि निपातत्वाऽभावादप्राप्ते विभाषेयम्' (this o is not a nipāta, so 1.1.15 could not give pragṛhya; hence the sutra); 'विष्णविति प्रगृह्यत्वाऽभावे रूपम्'.

overrides.note: when the samjna is taken, 6.1.125 keeps the o (viṣṇo iti); when not taken the ayādi goes ahead (viṣṇaviti / viṣṇa iti).

ordering_notes: The three-form result mixes a sapādasaptādhyāyī rule (6.1.78) with the tripādī optional 8.3.19 (lopaḥ śākalyasya), which acts last.

effect: According to Śākalya the particle uñ is optionally pragṛhya before the non-Vedic iti.
sthanin: no sound is replaced; optional samjna for the particle uñ (u with the marker ñ)
nimitta: the word is the particle uñ and the next word is the non-Vedic iti
conditions: Kasika: 'उञः प्रगृह्यसंज्ञा भवति इतौ शाकल्यस्याचार्यस्य मतेन। शाकल्यस्येति विभाषार्थम्'. The condition 'iti' and 'anārṣe' continue from 1.1.16 ('शाकल्यस्येतावनार्ष इति वर्तते').

Mahabhasya on this sutra: the nipāta u (no anubandha) is already nitya pragṛhya by 1.1.14; the sutra names uñ, the u with anubandha ñ ('द्वावुकाराविमौ। एकोऽननुबन्धकः। अपरः सानुबन्धकः').
ordering_notes: Balamanorama: the sutra pair 'उञः / ऊँ' is one sutra 'उञ ऊँ' in the Kasika, split by the Mahabhasya so that the 'viti' form (no samjna, no ādeśa) is obtainable ('अतो विभज्य व्याख्यातम्').

effect: According to Śākalya the particle uñ before non-Vedic iti is optionally replaced by ūm̐ (long, nasal, itself pragṛhya).
sthanin: the particle uñ (u)
adesa: ūm̐ (long ū with candrabindu), which is pragṛhya
nimitta: the next word is the non-Vedic iti; Śākalya's opinion
conditions: Kasika: 'उञ इतावनार्षे ऊँ इत्ययमादेशो भवति दीर्घोऽनुनासिकश्च शाकल्यस्य मतेन प्रगृह्यसंज्ञकश्च ... तेन त्रीणि रूपाणि भवन्ति। उ इति। विति। ऊँ इति'.
Balamanorama: 'एतदादेशाऽभावपक्षे पूर्वसूत्रेण प्रगृह्यत्वे सति उ इति रूपम्। प्रगृह्यत्वस्याप्यभावे सति यणादेशे विति'.

Tattvabodhini/Praudhamanorama on the wording: 'अनुनासिक इति। तेनास्मिन् परे यरोऽनुनासिके इति विकल्पः' - the anunāsika ūm̐ is mentioned so that 8.4.45 (yaro 'nunāsike 'nunāsiko vā) can act on a preceding yar (yad etad ūm̐ iti paṭhasi).
ordering_notes: Applies before 6.1.125 looks at the word (the substitute is itself pragṛhya).
optional: vibhasa (Śākalya): uñ -> ūm̐ or unchanged; overall three forms: ūm̐ iti, u iti, viti.
notes: The sutra text itself is 'ūm̐' = ū + m + combining candrabindu U+0310 in the Vidyut file; gold outputs use the same character sequence. Praudhamanorama on 8.3.33 shows that combined with 8.3.33 (v), 8.4.57 and 8.4.47 there are dozens of forms (28) of 'kim u iti'; those are not modelled.

effect: An ī or ū (word-final) that stands for the meaning of the locative case is pragṛhya.
sthanin: no sound is replaced; samjna for an ī/ū-ending word whose case ending was elided (sup-luk) but which still expresses the locative
nimitta: the word ends in ī or ū and stands for a locative (gaurī = gauryām, māmakī = māmakyām, tanū = tanvām); the locative ending is elided (7.1.39 supāṃ sulug ...)
conditions: Kasika: 'ईदन्तमूदन्तं च शब्दरूपं सप्तम्यर्थे वर्तमानं प्रगृह्यसंज्ञं भवति'; examples 'अध्यस्यां मामकी तनू', 'सोमो गौरी अधि श्रितः'. The condition 'anārṣe/Śākalya' of 1.1.16 does NOT continue ('शाकल्यस्येतावनार्षे इति निवृत्तम्').

'ईदूताविति किम्?' (Rg 5.37.5 'priyaḥ sūrye priyo agnā bhavāti', the e/ā locatives are not covered); 'सप्तमीग्रहणं किम्? धीती, मती, सुष्टुती' (Vedic instrumentals in ī: not covered); 'अर्थग्रहणं किम्? वाप्यश्वः। नद्यातिः' (a compound has passed to another meaning).

Balamanorama: 'अर्थग्रहणाद्यत्र सप्तम्या लुकियः शिष्यते स लुप्यमानार्थाभिधायी इति न्यायेन प्रकृतेरेव सप्तम्यर्थे पर्यवसानम्' - the sutra applies only where the case ending has been elided and the STEM itself carries the locative sense; real locatives in ī/ū with an ending (e.g. vātapramī) are not examples.

Mahabhasya: without 'artha' the compound member could also count (vāpyaśvaḥ); with it the word must remain 'jahatsvārtha' or stay within the sense of the seventh case; the Mahabhasya's verse: 'ईदूतौ सप्तमीत्येव लुप्तेऽर्थग्रहणाद् भवेत्। पूर्वस्य चेत्सवर्णोऽसावाडाम्भावः प्रसज्यते'.
ordering_notes: The elision of the locative ending (7.1.39) must already have taken place; 1.1.62 pratyayalakṣaṇa would otherwise undo it (Mahabhasya: 'न प्रगृह्यसञ्ज्ञायां प्रत्ययलक्षणं भवति' is the jñāpaka drawn from the wording of this sutra).

varttikas.text: ईदूतौ सप्तमीत्येव लुप्तेऽर्थग्रहणाद् भवेत् । पूर्वस्य चेत्सवर्णोऽसावाडाम्भावः प्रसज्यते
varttikas.source: Kasika on 1.1.19 (kārikā of the Mahabhasya, verse 1)

notes: ENGINE: flag saptamyartha (i/u standing for a locative). All attested examples are Vedic (Rg 9.12.3, Paippalada Samhita 1.6.8) although the sutra has no 'chandasi'; tier 'vedic'. Not in Laghu.

effect: Heading: everything from here up to (but excluding) the ī of 'adhirīśvare' (1.4.97) is called nipāta.
sthanin: no substitution
nimitta: the range of sutras 1.4.57-1.4.96
conditions: Kasika: 'प्रागेतस्मादवधेर्यानित ऊर्ध्वमनुक्रमिष्यामः निपातसंज्ञास्ते वेदितव्याः ... प्राग्वचनं संज्ञासमावेशार्थम्'; the 'r' of 'rīśvara' stops the limit from being 'īśvare tosunkasunau' (3.4.13): 'रेफोच्चारणम् ईश्वरे तोसुन्कसुनौ इत्ययमवधिर्मा विज्ञायीति'.
ordering_notes: The nipāta samjna may coexist with gati, upasarga and karmapravacanīya samjñā ('गत्युपसर्गकर्मप्रवचनीयसंज्ञाभिस्सह निपातसंज्ञा समाविशति').
notes: Balamanorama calls it an 'anantaka' sutra ('अनन्तकमिदं सूत्रम्'). Not in Laghu. Pure vocabulary rule; no sandhi effect. Kasika verse: 'रीश्वराद्वीस्वरान्मा भूत् कृन्मेजन्तः परोऽपि सः। समासेष्वव्ययीभावो लौकिकं चातिवर्तते' (Mahabhasya 1.4.56 vartikas 1-4).

effect: The cādi words (ca, vā, ha, aha, eva, ... a, i, u, ṛ, ḷ, e, ai, o, au ... iti, iva ...) are called nipāta, provided they do not denote a substance.
sthanin: no substitution; samjna to the members of the cādi list
nimitta: the word is in the ganapatha 'cādi' and denotes an action/relation (asattva) rather than a thing (dravya)
conditions: Kasika: 'चादयो निपातसंज्ञा भवन्ति, न चेत्सत्त्वे वर्तन्ते। प्रसज्यप्रतिषेधोऽयम्, सत्त्वमिति द्रव्यमुच्यते'; 'असत्वे इति किम्? पशुर्वै पुरुषः। पशुः पुरोडाशः' (paśu as an animal is a dravya).
Balamanorama: 'लिङ्गसङ्ख्याकारकान्वितं द्रव्यम्'; 'इह तु स्यादेव - पुष्टं पशु मन्यते' (paśu in the sense of 'well').

Kasika adds the vowels a i u ṛ ḷ e ai o au and the class 'उपसर्गविभक्तिस्वरप्रतिरूपकाश्च निपाताः' as members; prādi (1.4.58) too. The list is an ākṛtigaṇa (open ended): corpus.ganas_for('1.4.57') marks open_ended=True.
Vidyut ganapatha cādi list: 155 items; single vowels among them: a, i, u, ṛ, ḷ, u, e, ai, o, au; o-ending: o, āho, utāho, ho, aho, no, atho.
ordering_notes: Comes first in the derivation of a pragṛhya nipāta: cādi membership -> nipāta (1.4.57) -> 1.1.14/1.1.15 -> pragṛhya -> 6.1.125.
notes: GRETIL prints the sutra as "cādayo 'satve" (vlk_53 = p_1,4.57): the text has a typo (asatve for asattve) but the tag is right. Nipāta samjña also feeds 1.1.37 (svarādinipātamavyayam) etc. The Kasika list and the Vidyut list differ in spelling and order; use the Vidyut gana in the engine.

effect: The prādi words (pra, parā, apa, sam, anu, ava, nis, nir, dus, dur, vi, āṅ, ni, adhi, api, ati, su, ud, abhi, prati, pari, upa) are also called nipāta (when not denoting a substance).
sthanin: no substitution; samjna to the members of the prādi list
nimitta: the word is in the prādi list and does not denote a substance
conditions: Kasika: 'प्रादयोऽसत्त्वे निपातसंज्ञा भवन्ति ... पृथग्योगकरणमुत्तरसंज्ञाविशेषणार्थम्। उपसर्गाः क्रियायोगे इति चादीनामुपसर्गसंज्ञा मा भूत्' (the separate sutra makes sure the cādi words do not become upasargas); 'असत्त्व इत्येव - परा जयन्ति सेनाः' (parā as a verb-form, not a prādi).
Vidyut prādi list (corpus.ganas_for('1.4.58'), closed): pra, parā, apa, sam, anu, ava, nis, nir, dus, dur, vi, āṅ, ni, adhi, api, ati, su, ud, abhi, prati, pari, upa.
Laghu: 'एतेऽपि तथा'.
notes: Relevance for pragṛhya: the single-vowel prādi is only 'āṅ' (ā), which is excluded when ṅit (1.1.14). The corpus attaches the two vartikas ('marut', 'śra') to this sutra; the Kasika/Mahabhasya place them under 1.4.59. Balamanorama's entry for 1.4.58 in the corpus is an empty heading.

effect: When joined with an action (kriyāyoga), the prādi words are called upasarga.
sthanin: no substitution; samjna to prādi words joined to a verb (or verbal noun)
nimitta: a prādi word that is connected with a verbal action (kriyāyoga)
conditions: Kasika: 'प्रादयः क्रियायोगे उपसर्गसंज्ञा भवन्ति। प्रणयति। परिणयति। प्रणायकः। परिणायकः'; 'क्रियायोग इति किम्? प्रगतो नायकोऽस्माद्देशात् प्रनायको देशः'.
The upasarga samjna is what enables ṇatva 8.4.14, ṣatva 8.3.65, vṛddhi 6.1.91, ekādeśa 6.1.94 etc. (Kasika: 'उपसर्गप्रदेशाः - उपसर्गे घोः किः इत्येवमादयः').
Laghu lists the members: pra parā apa sam anu ava nis nir dus dur vi āṅ ni adhi api ati su ut abhi prati pari upa (22, the prādi list).

varttikas.source: Kasika on 1.4.59 (Mahabhasya 1.4.59 vartika 2): marut counts as upasarga: maruttaḥ (marudbhir dattaḥ)
Kasika on 1.4.59 (Mahabhasya vartika 3): śrat counts: śraddhā (ātaś copasarge 3.3.106)

notes: For the sandhi engine the upasarga samjna is boundary information (boundary 'upasarga', flag 'upasarga' in gold). Balamanorama has no entry for this sutra in the corpus; its 1.4.60 entry treats both sutras together. Praudhamanoramā's entry on 1.4.59 is only a note on nis/dus versus nir/dur (Vamana, Haradatta) that closes the samjñāprakaraṇa.

effect: The same prādi words, when joined with an action, are ALSO called gati (in addition to upasarga).
sthanin: no substitution; samjna 'gati' to prādi words joined to an action
nimitta: the prādi word is connected with a verbal action
conditions: Kasika: 'गतिसंज्ञकाश्च प्रादयो भवन्ति क्रियायोगे'; the 'ca' brings about coexistence with the upasarga samjna ('चकारः संज्ञासमावेशार्थः'): praṇītam, abhiṣiktam get both the gati accent rules (6.2.49 gatiranantaraḥ) and the upasarga rules ṇatva 8.4.14 and ṣatva 8.3.65.
'योगविभाग उत्तरार्थः' - the separate sutra ensures only gati (not upasarga) for later items, e.g. 'ūrīsyāt' and 8.3.87 (upasargapradurbhyām astir yacparaḥ) would otherwise apply.

Laghu (in the declension of dhī): the vartika '(gatikāraketarapūrvapadasya yaṇ neṣyate)' -> śuddhadhiyau: for a compound whose first member is neither gati nor kāraka the yaṇ of 6.4.82 is not wanted (the dual is śuddhadhiyau).
notes: Laghu vlk_202 (line 460 of the GRETIL text) sits in the dhī/bhrū declension, not in the sandhi chapters: hence tier 'support'. GRETIL tag p_1,4.60 is right. Kasika vartikas: 'kārikāśabdasyopasaṅkhyānam', 'punaś canasau chandasi', 'duraḥ ṣatvaṇatvayor upasargatvapratiṣedho vaktavyaḥ'. The dur-vartika means duṣ-kṛtam etc. do not get upasarga-ṇatva/ṣatva from 'dur' (Kasika 'निस्सान्तौ दुस्सान्तौ').

effect: Inside an Rk-pāda, an eṅ (e or o) word-final stays unchanged before a short a that is not followed by v or y.
sthanin: the pūrvarūpa that 6.1.109 would produce; the e/o itself stays
adesa: prakṛtibhāva: e/o remain, the following a is pronounced separately
nimitta: e or o at the end of a pada, standing INSIDE an Rk-pāda (antaḥpāda), and the following short a is not followed by v or y
conditions: Kasika: 'एङ इति यत् पञ्चम्यन्तमनुवर्तते, तदर्थादिह प्रथमान्तं भवति ... पादशब्देन च ऋक्पादस्यैव ग्रहणमिष्यते, न तु श्लोकपादस्य। अवकारयकारपरेऽति परत एङ् प्रकृत्या भवति'.
'अन्तः पादमिति किम्? कया मती कुत एतास एतेऽर्चन्ति' (across a pāda boundary: pūrvarūpa); 'अव्यपर इति किम्? तेऽवदन्। तेजोऽयस्मयम्'; 'एङिति किम्? अन्वग्निरुषसामग्रमख्यत्'.
Kaumudi: 'ऋक्पादमध्यस्थ एङ् प्रकृत्या स्यादति परे न तु वकारयकारपरेऽति'.

Kasika records a rival reading 'नान्तःपादमव्यपरे' whose sense is a general prohibition of everything 'संहितायामिह यदुच्यते तस्य सर्वस्य प्रतिषेधम्'; Mahabhasya reads 'नान्तः पादमव्यपरे' and discusses the over-application (vartika 1: 'नान्तःपादमिति सर्वप्रतिषेधश्चेदतिप्रसङ्गः' - anvagniruṣasām would be affected).

exceptions_and_blockers.note: the 'avyapare' exclusion is lifted for the listed words (avyāt, avadyāt, avakramuḥ, avrata, ayam, avantu, avasyu).

overrides.note: instead of eṅaḥ padāntād ati (pūrvarūpa) the e/o stays: Kasika 'स्वभावेनावतिष्ठते ... न विकारमापद्यते'.

ordering_notes: The condition 'antaḥpāda' and the a-not-before-v/y check look at the word after 8.2.x has not yet acted (6.1.113 ato roraplutād aplute makes the o from ru first; the o then meets this sutra).

varttikas.source: Mahabhasya on 6.1.115 (vartika 1, on the reading 'nāntaḥ pādam')

notes: ENGINE: needs the Vedic pāda structure and the Kasika's ‘a not followed by v/y’ test; letters alone cannot say whether the o is inside a pāda. Reading disagreement: Vidyut/Kasika 'prakṛtyā''ntaḥpādam avyapare' vs Mahabhasya 'nāntaḥ pādam avyapare' (Tattvabodhini/Praudhamanorama on 6.1.122 note that the Mahabhasya reading is 'नान्तः पादम्' and that with it 6.1.122 'सर्वत्र विभाषा गोः' would optionalise the pūrvarūpa instead of the prakṛtibhāva). Not in Laghu.

effect: In the seven listed words (avyāt, avadyāt, avakramuḥ, avrata, ayam, avantu, avasyu) the eṅ stays even though the a is followed by v or y.
sthanin: the pūrvarūpa of 6.1.109 (and the 'avyapare' exception of 6.1.115)
adesa: prakṛtibhāva of the e/o before these words
nimitta: e/o at the end of a pada inside an Rk-pāda, before a-initial avyāt, avadyāt, avakramuḥ, avrata, ayam, avantu, avasyu
conditions: Kasika: 'अव्यात् अवद्यात् अवक्रमुः अव्रत अयम् अवन्तु अवस्यु इत्येतेषु वकारयकारपरेऽप्यति परतोऽन्तः पादमेङ् प्रकृत्या भवति'.
Kaumudi: 'यद्यपि बह्वृचैस्तेनोऽवन्तु, रथतूः, सोऽयमगात्, तेऽरुणेभिरित्यादौ प्रकृतिभावो न क्रियते तथापि बाहुलकात्समाधेयम्। प्रातिशाख्ये तु वाचनिक एवायमर्थः'.

overrides.note: lifts its 'avyapare' restriction for these words.
same as 6.1.115: prakṛtibhāva instead of pūrvarūpa.

notes: Kaumudi lists the Rk/Yajus examples 'vasubhir no avyāt', 'mitramaho avadyāt' (the Kaumudi print reads 'मिमहो'), 'mā śivāso avakramuḥ', 'te no avrata', 'śatadhāro ayam maṇiḥ', 'te no 'vantu', 'kuśikāso avasyavaḥ'; the Bahvrca reading of 'te no 'vantu' etc. does not show prakṛtibhāva (Kaumudi 'बाहुलकात्').

effect: In the Yajus the word uro (uraḥ) stays unchanged before a, without the antaḥpāda condition.
sthanin: the pūrvarūpa of 6.1.109
adesa: prakṛtibhāva of the eṅ-final uro before short a
nimitta: Yajurveda usage; the word uraḥ (eṅ-final uro) before a
conditions: Kasika: 'उरःशब्द एङन्तो यजुषि विषयेऽति प्रकृत्या भवति। उरो अन्तरिक्षम्'; 'यजुषि पादानामभावादनन्तःपादार्थं वचनम्'.
Kasika records a variant sutra 'यजुष्युरो' with the vocative of uru: 'उरो अन्तरिक्षे सजूः'.

overrides.note: prakṛtibhāva instead of pūrvarūpa.

notes: Vedic and accent-dependent (Yajus); not in Laghu.

effect: In the Yajus the words āpo, juṣāṇo, vṛṣṇo, varṣiṣṭhe, and ambe, ambāle (the ones before ambikā) stay unchanged before a.
sthanin: the pūrvarūpa of 6.1.109
adesa: prakṛtibhāva of these eṅ-final words before short a
nimitta: Yajus; the listed words āpaḥ, juṣāṇaḥ, vṛṣṇaḥ, varṣiṣṭhe, ambe, ambāle (ambike being the third)
conditions: Kasika: 'आपो जुषाणो वृष्णो वर्षिष्ठे इत्येते शब्दा अम्बे अम्बाले इत्येतौ च यावम्बिकेशब्दात् पूर्वौ यजुषि पठितौ तेऽति परतः प्रकृत्या भवन्ति'.
Kasika: 'अस्मादेव निपातनाद् अम्बार्थनद्योर्ह्रस्वः इति ह्रस्वत्वं न भवति' (7.3.107 is not applied to ambe).

notes: Yajus only; the words are given in their pausal/vocative forms (āpo = āpaḥ + a).

effect: In the Yajus the eṅ inside the word aṅga (aṅge) and the eṅ before the a that begins 'aṅga' stay unchanged before a.
sthanin: the pūrvarūpa of 6.1.109
nimitta: Yajus; the e/o is the eṅ of aṅga (aṅge) followed by a, or precedes the initial a of the word aṅga
conditions: Kasika: 'अङ्गशब्दे य एङ् तदादौ चाकारे यः पूर्वः स यजुषि विषयेऽति प्रकृत्या भवति। ऐन्द्रः प्राणो अङ्गेअङ्गे अदीध्यत्'.
Kaumudi: 'प्राणो अङ्गे अङ्गे अदीध्यत्'.

notes: Yajus only.

effect: In the Yajus an eṅ stays before an anudātta a that is followed by a kavarga letter or dh.
sthanin: the pūrvarūpa of 6.1.109
nimitta: Yajus; e/o before an anudātta short a which is itself followed by k kh g gh ṅ or dh
conditions: Kasika: 'अनुदात्ते चाति कवर्गधकारपरे परतो यजुषि विषय एङ् प्रकृत्या भवति। अयं नो अग्निः। अयं सो अध्वरः'.
